speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to Sorcery.
zh: 欢迎来到 Sorcery。

speaker: Unknown
en: The potential of photonics.
zh: 光子学的潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: The technology to interconnect these GPUs.
zh: 互联这些 GPU 的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Global payroll and HR platform.
zh: 全球薪酬与人力资源平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Eight billion operational data points.
zh: 八十亿个运营数据点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Scale ups over startups.
zh: 规模化成长公司胜过初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'd rather have a million of something than one of anything.
zh: 你宁愿拥有一百万个某种东西，也不愿只拥有一个任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Building the intelligence layer for defense.
zh: 为国防构建智能层。

speaker: Unknown
en: There isn't enough power.
zh: 电力不够了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's not enough memory chips.
zh: 内存芯片不够了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're at the end of physics of what we can still do.
zh: 我们已经到了物理学上还能做的事情的尽头。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're on our final talk for today.
zh: 那么我们今天进行的是最后一场演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, we have Steven and we have Adam.
zh: 今天，我们有 Steven 和 Adam。

speaker: Unknown
en: Steven, you come from iMac.
zh: Steven，你来自 iMac。

speaker: Unknown
en: Adam, you're from Strike.
zh: Adam，你来自 Strike。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're going to talk a little bit about what comes after the GPU.
zh: 所以我们要聊一聊 GPU 之后会是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's start with you.
zh: 那么先从你开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you explain what iMac is?
zh: 你能解释一下 iMac 是什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're a little bit the most unknown hidden gem in semiconductors, at least unknown for the average Joe, definitely not unknown for the semiconductor world itself.
zh: 我觉得我们有点像半导体领域最不为人知的隐藏宝石，至少对普通人来说是未知的，但在半导体行业本身绝对不是未知的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're the worldwide leader in chips, but in actually the early stages of building a chip.
zh: 我们是芯片领域的全球领导者，但处于芯片制造的非常早期阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: So hardware is not like software.
zh: 硬件不像软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that you're prompted and suddenly 30 seconds later, something comes out of it.
zh: 不是你输入提示词，三十秒后结果就出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it's a process of five to 10 years.
zh: 不，这是一个五到十年的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're at a very early stage of that process where we have a unique clean room facility that nobody else in the world has.
zh: 而我们处于这个过程的非常早期阶段，我们拥有一间世界上独一无二的洁净室设施，世界上没有其他人有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so all the biggest ship providers in the world actually first come to us, first in Belgium,
zh: 所以世界上所有最大的芯片提供商实际上都会先来找我们，先到比利时，

speaker: Unknown
en: To kind of design that next generation chip that you'll see maybe in 7, 8 to 10 years from now.
zh: 来设计那种你可能在未来七、八年到十年才会看到的新一代芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: And going through a whole phase of designing that chip, we hand it over then to them to further commercialize it.
zh: 在经历整个芯片设计阶段后，我们再把它交给他们去进一步商业化。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in that sense, there's almost no chip in the world today that has not been touched by iMac in some way.
zh: 但从这个意义上说，今天世界上几乎没有任何一颗芯片没有在某种程度上被 iMac 触及过。

speaker: Unknown
en: We already exist for 40 years and we've been driven more or less that chip roadmap for the last 40 years.
zh: 我们已经存在了 40 年，并且在过去 40 年里，我们或多或少一直在推动芯片路线图。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I should have asked you the secret question, because you know all the secrets on chips.
zh: 那我本应该问你那个秘密问题，因为你了解所有芯片的秘密。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of them I'm allowed to answer.
zh: 其中一些我是被允许回答的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What can you answer?
zh: 你能回答什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think we're definitely going to talk more about that, but indeed that we're actually seeing a huge amount of disruptions going on.
zh: 嗯，我觉得我们确实会更多地谈到这个，但确实，我们正在看到大量颠覆正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're now kind of plateauing in what we call Moore's law.
zh: 我觉得我们现在在所谓的摩尔定律上有点进入平台期了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean?
zh: 这是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: Chips have been becoming bigger and bigger or faster and faster over the last years.
zh: 在过去这些年里，芯片变得越来越大、越来越快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We always did that through scaling.
zh: 我们一直都是通过缩放做到这一点的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what does that mean?
zh: 那这是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: It means that we made the transistor smaller and smaller.
zh: 这意味着我们把晶体管做得越来越小。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're at the level that a transistor has about the depth of one nanometer.
zh: 而我们现在已经到了晶体管深度大约只有一纳米的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is one nanometer?
zh: 一纳米是多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about 100,000 times smaller than a human hair.
zh: 大约是一根人类头发的一万分之一小。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means that we're at the end of physics of what we can still do.
zh: 那意味着我们已经到了物理学上还能做的事情的尽头。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we're going to come into an era where...
zh: 而且我认为我们将进入一个时代……

speaker: Unknown
en: What we do in hardware needs to be way more inventive than what we've been doing in the last 10 to 20 years to keep on scaling that roadmap of more to make sure that chips become faster and faster as they already did the last four decades basically.
zh: 我们在硬件上所做的事情，需要比过去十到二十年所做的更有创造性，才能继续推进那条缩放路线图，确保芯片像过去基本四十年那样变得越来越快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Adam, as you look into the chip industry, how do you make sense of it?
zh: Adam，当你审视芯片行业时，你是怎么理解它的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you map it out?
zh: 你是怎么把它梳理清楚的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think right now GPUs are very good at the training part and we're now looking at the bottleneck that sits in the inference layer and the bottlenecks that I look at the most and try and look at companies that attack those bottlenecks sit in power and energy, memory, cooling and data transfer.
zh: 是的，我认为现在 GPU 在训练部分非常擅长，我们现在正关注位于推理层的瓶颈，而我关注最多的瓶颈、并试图寻找攻克这些瓶颈的公司的那些环节，存在于电力和能源、内存、散热以及数据传输方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we look at the inference side of things, the memory shortage in general and increasing the bandwidth and lowering the latency of getting the useful memory to a GPU as quick as possible is a really interesting and exciting place that needs to be builded within.
zh: 所以当我们看推理这一侧，整体上的内存短缺，以及提高带宽、降低延迟、让有用的内存尽可能快地到达 GPU，是一个非常有趣且令人兴奋、需要在其中进行建设的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cooling as well and where that's going.
zh: 还有散热，以及散热的发展方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think bringing the liquid that takes heat away from the chip closer and closer to the GPU itself is how it's going to progress over the next five to 10 years.
zh: 我认为，把带走芯片热量的液体带得离 GPU 本身越来越近，就是它未来五到十年的演进方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of the value will go to the manufacturing side of that.
zh: 而且我认为，很多价值将流向这方面的制造端。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, I mean, power, everyone knows how much of a constraint and a bottleneck that is and increasing the capacity there is huge.
zh: 是的，我是说，电力，大家都知道那是多大的制约和瓶颈，提高这方面的容量是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I recently interviewed Tony Kim of BlackRock at the RAISE AI Summit.
zh: 我最近在 RAISE AI 峰会上采访了 BlackRock 的 Tony Kim。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually in Paris.
zh: 实际上是在巴黎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're talking about hardware.
zh: 我们在谈硬件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the hardware era, Renaissance, everything's shifting to hardware.
zh: 就像是硬件时代、文艺复兴，一切都在转向硬件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Software is getting...
zh: 软件正在变得……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's taking a bit of a beating, but the margins, people don't understand, the margins for chips are fantastic and for hardware versus software, which is getting eaten by AI and again, like the token spend and that kind of thing.
zh: 软件正受到一点打击，但利润率，人们不理解，芯片的利润率好得惊人，硬件相对于软件而言，后者正被 AI 蚕食，又是 token 支出之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you make sense of the shift in value and how like the pyramid kind of flipped?
zh: 那么你如何理解价值的转移，以及金字塔如何翻转的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think the demand is just so high for the thing that is less fruitful out there, right?
zh: 嗯，我认为只是因为那个最不富余的东西需求太高了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there isn't enough power.
zh: 所以电力不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's not enough memory chips.
zh: 内存芯片不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: The shortage in memory, I mean, if we look at, there's only three companies in the world that produce memory, which is 95% of the market, Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung.
zh: 内存的短缺，我是说，如果我们看看，世界上只有三家公司生产内存，占 95% 的市场，美光、SK 海力士和三星。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two of them are in Korea.
zh: 其中两家在韩国。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of their shift has
zh: 而且它们的很多转变

speaker: Unknown
en: been filled out by hyperscalers taking over their whole inventory.
zh: 已经被超大规模云厂商占据其全部库存所填补。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've seen prices rise by 700% this year just for the memory part of the chip.
zh: 所以你看到今年仅芯片的内存部分价格就上涨了 700%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that will happen across the layer because it's the thing that's in the most demand.
zh: 而且这会发生在整个层的各个部分，因为这是需求最大的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The training side and the software side of things is continually getting better, but the physical side is the thing that's harder to get better overnight.
zh: 训练侧和软件侧在不断变好，但物理这一侧是很难一夜之间变好的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, to be honest, I don't really think it's necessarily flipped.
zh: 是的，说实话，我真的不认为它一定翻转了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's more the immaturity of the software market right now.
zh: 我认为这更多是当前软件市场的不成熟。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might seem weird that I say immaturity of the software market, but I think what we've been doing at AI the last four or five years has, of course, in software been tremendous.
zh: 我说软件市场不成熟可能听起来很奇怪，但我认为我们过去四五年在 AI 上所做的，当然在软件方面是了不起的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you look at it from, okay, how complex it is to actually, in terms of computations, do whatever...
zh: 但如果你从这个角度看，好吧，从计算的角度来说，真正做到……

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, large language models can do.
zh: 我是说，大语言模型能做到的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still very much a brute force approach.
zh: 它仍然在很大程度上是一种暴力破解的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a result, the value that you can get out of it is pretty limited.
zh: 因此，你能从中获得的价值是相当有限的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if you're going to get further, we're going to see new types of software evolutions as well, which are tied way more closer to hardware.
zh: 而且我认为，如果要走得更远，我们也会看到新类型的软件演进，它们与硬件的联系要紧密得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because of that, I think the value will increase way bigger.
zh: 正因为如此，我认为价值将会大幅增加。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think so we're kind of filling the base of that pyramid already in hardware of creating a lot of value there.
zh: 而且我认为，我们其实已经在硬件方面填充了那个金字塔的底部，在那里创造了大量价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think software will follow in that sense.
zh: 我认为软件在那个意义上会跟上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing more and more chip companies founded every year, probably than ever before.
zh: 我们看到每年成立的芯片公司比以往任何时候都多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And venture dollars are definitely helping fund that.
zh: 而且风投资金肯定在帮助资助这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a capacity to how many chips can exist in the market?
zh: 市场上能存在的芯片数量有上限吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think right now there's kind of endless demand for that.
zh: 我认为目前这方面的需求几乎是无限的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's still going to be the question of how that can continue.
zh: 而且我认为这仍然会是一个问题，即这种情况如何能持续。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's rather the bottleneck is manufacturing, manufacturing the right type of components in different regions.
zh: 我认为瓶颈反而在制造，在不同地区制造正确类型的组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think, for example, what Temma Foundries is doing there is super important, but having the right type of components for that is I think the real bottleneck, not necessarily the number of companies that do this because every company can come with
zh: 而且我认为，例如，Temma Foundries 在这方面做的超级重要，但拥有正确类型的组件才是真正的瓶颈，而不一定是做这件事的公司数量，因为每家公司都可以带来

speaker: Unknown
en: A completely different, unique design.
zh: 完全不同的、独特的设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that sense can also kind of revolutionize what we're going to have as well.
zh: 从这个意义上说，也可以在一定程度上革新我们将拥有的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And probably in the software world, we're going to see way more different types of algorithms.
zh: 而且在软件世界，我们可能会看到更多不同类型的算法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a result, we will also need more diversification in the type of hardware.
zh: 因此，我们也需要硬件类型上更多的多样化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So more than just GPUs as well.
zh: 所以也不仅仅是 GPU。

speaker: Unknown
en: As models get bigger and bigger, what breaks first on the chip layer?
zh: 随着模型变得越来越大，芯片层上什么会先坏掉？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, yeah, I think for sure right now memory.
zh: 嗯，是的，我认为现在肯定是内存。

speaker: Unknown
en: Memory is absolutely the number one component that is already broken today.
zh: 内存绝对是今天已经坏掉的头号组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't really think that models will become necessarily bigger and bigger.
zh: 但我真的不认为模型一定会变得越来越大。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you just think about it, the latest open source models like KimiK3D already have more parameters.
zh: 如果你只是想一想，最新的开源模型比如 KimiK3D 已经拥有更多参数，

speaker: Unknown
en: than what the human brain has.
zh: 超过人脑所拥有的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But on the other hand, that K3 chip that we need to fuel that K3 model is about a million times more or less energy efficient than what the human brain is.
zh: 但另一方面，我们需要用来驱动那个 K3 模型的 K3 芯片，在能效上大约比人脑低了一百万倍左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think we're going to see a different type of...
zh: 所以我认为我们会看到一种不同类型的……

speaker: Unknown
en: Of paradigm, we kind of went into an era the last five years of building bigger and bigger and bigger models.
zh: 范式。过去五年我们某种程度上进入了建造越来越大的模型的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: We went from 175 billion parameters to kind of 10 trillion parameters right now.
zh: 我们从 1750 亿参数走到了现在差不多 10 万亿参数。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's going to stop.
zh: 这会停止。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a lot of companies right now taking that shift as we speak, abandoning what we call the scaling hypothesis of building bigger and bigger models and therefore trying to solve those memory bottlenecks as well.
zh: 现在有很多公司正在发生这种转变，放弃我们所说的越建越大模型的扩展假设，因此也在尝试解决那些内存瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Copper has kind of met its days.
zh: 铜的时代差不多到头了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious, how do you think about photonics and how that changes the layer?
zh: 我很好奇，你怎么看光子学，以及它如何改变这一层？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, feel free to... Yeah, I mean, I think there are so many benefits to using photonics instead of copper and...
zh: 好的，我的意思是，请随意……好的，我的意思是，我认为用光子学代替铜有非常多的好处，而且……

speaker: Unknown
en: Copper is easy because it's all in electrical, it's all digital.
zh: 铜很简单，因为它全是电的，全是数字的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the bottleneck with photonics is changing between optical and the electrical layer.
zh: 而光子学的瓶颈在于光层和电层之间的转换。

speaker: Unknown
en: But transferring data more quickly and more efficiently and not having that latent heat aspect that electrons and copper wires do will only continue to scale the efficiency of data transfer.
zh: 但更快、更高效地传输数据，并且没有电子在铜线中那样的潜在发热问题，只会持续提升数据传输的效率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think we'll see the architecture continually shift
zh: 然后我认为我们会看到架构持续转变，

speaker: Unknown
en: for where photonics will be within data centers.
zh: 关于光子学在数据中心里所处的位置。 [[106——原文如此]] 目前它是在集群之间，我们使用线性可插拔光模块，但我认为在未来五年我们会看到这些光学组件越来越接近实际的 GPU，我们会走向共封装光学的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the moment it's between the clusters and we're using linear pluggable optics, but I think in the next five years we will see these optical components get closer and closer to the actual GPU and we will go towards a state of co-packaged optics.
zh: 目前它位于集群之间，我们使用的是线性可插拔光模块，但我认为在未来五年内，我们会看到这些光学元件越来越接近实际的 GPU，我们将走向共封装光学的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for me, I mean, every day what I do actually at iMac is thinking about what could be AI in the future.
zh: 对我来说，我的意思是，我每天在 iMac 实际做的事情就是思考未来 AI 可能是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how is AI going to evolve in like five to 10 years from now?
zh: 也就是 AI 在比如从现在起五到十年会如何演化？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we're seeing kind of from a software perspective that very much diversifying path of
zh: 我认为我们从软件的角度正在看到一条非常多元的路径，

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of different approaches, whether it's world models or more reinforcement learning based approaches.
zh: 很多不同的方法，无论是世界模型还是更多基于强化学习的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what is 100% clear is that whatever scenario in the end will become the dominating model of the future, moving data...
zh: 但百分之百清楚的是，无论最终哪种场景会成为未来的主导模型，移动数据……

speaker: Unknown
en: As fast as possible in the quickest way with the huge amounts of data that we need to shift is always going to be what we need because again, towards the analogy of the human brain, that's what our human brain is also unbelievably good at.
zh: 以最快的方式尽快地移动我们需要传输的海量数据，永远会是我们所需要的，因为再次用人脑的类比，这正是我们人脑也极其擅长的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have an unbelievable 3D structure that is able to do this.
zh: 我们有一个难以置信的 3D 结构能够做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so photonics will play, I think for me, especially in the next years, it's going to be the killer technology to enable the chips of the future.
zh: 所以光子学将会——对我来说，尤其是在接下来的几年——成为实现未来芯片的关键技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think also on photonics, it's attacking many parts of the bottlenecks that I touched on at the start.
zh: 我还认为在光子学方面，它正在攻克我在开头提到的许多瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's attacking energy because it can transfer data quicker.
zh: 它攻克能源，因为它能更快地传输数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's attacking cooling because you don't need as much cooling around these GPUs if you're transferring through light.
zh: 它攻克散热，因为如果你通过光传输，就不需要在这些 GPU 周围配置那么多散热。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it's attacking data transfer at the core.
zh: 而且它在最核心处攻克数据传输。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think having spanning most of the bottlenecks that we're seeing in the AI Infra build out right now, it's like the key technology that is likely to win.
